@@ -104,6 +114,10 @@ pub fn next_step(
         return Verdict::Replan { stale_chunks };
     }
 
+    // A decision settles what the reviewer had read when they made it, and
+    // says nothing about a batch written since. It must not stand in for
+    // reading one: this is the gate the whole design rests on, and letting a
+    // decision retire it would let an agent write the entire plan unread.
     let unreviewed = spec
         .chunks
         .iter()

overview.intent: Stop an approve or comment decision from ending a harness review that has not yet written every change into a chunk, so settling one batch lets the harness carry on to the next instead of completing.
changes: In `next_step` (crates/gewu-review/src/harness/progress.rs), an Approve or Comment decision returns `Verdict::Complete` up front only when every change in the current manifest already appears in some chunk of the spec; otherwise the decision is ignored at that point and the remaining gates (requests, re-plan, waiting for unread chunks, expand) run as usual.
The set of written change IDs is now computed once at the top of `next_step` as `written` and reused by the drift check, replacing the later `expanded` set with identical contents.

The review TUI's summary screen no longer asks for confirmation when unwritten changes remain: `finish_review` records the derived outcome directly, and the `unwritten()` helper and its test are deleted. The footer and summary text that still say "End the review" were not changed by this diff.

New domain tests cover: completion when everything is written, waiting for an unread batch despite a decision, expanding after approving a partial review, and a Code request still routing to handover after a Comment decision. Runner tests are split the same way. These tests were read, not executed, in this investigation.
concepts: Batch: the chunks the harness has appended to the spec since the reviewer last read; the harness writes the review a work item at a time and waits between batches.

Verdict / `next_step`: the pure domain function that decides what `gewu harness next` does — Expand, Wait, Replan, Handover, Revise, or Complete — from the spec, the reviewer's session, the work list, and the current and previous manifests.

Decision: the session's recorded Approve, Comment, or RequestChanges, derived in the TUI from the reviewer's feedback (`ReviewSession::outcome`) rather than chosen; it persists in the session event log until another decision event overwrites it.
Written (formerly `expanded`): the set of manifest change IDs that some chunk in the spec already quotes.

chunks.title: The wait gate is documented as outranking a decision
chunks.summary: Only a comment is added above the unreviewed-chunk count; the count itself is unchanged. It states that a decision must not substitute for reading a batch written after it.

content.markdown: Check this comment against the early return in “Completion now also requires every change to be written”. `ReviewSession::apply` overwrites `decision` only on another `DecisionSet` event, and the harness keys the session by `review_id`, so an Approve from batch 1 is still recorded when later batches arrive. Once the final item is appended, `whole` becomes true: does `gewu harness next` then return Complete before this count is reached, leaving the last batch unread?

chunks.confidence: Read from source only; no test or run here exercises a decision recorded before the final batch is written.
